newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SES likely to investigate Lum Chang.
newsitem.headline: SES likely to investigate Lum Chang.

text.p: The Stock Exchange of Singapore (SES) is likely to launch its own investigation into charges of insider trading by Singapore businessman Raymond Lum Kwan Sung, market sources said on Monday.
Lum is chairman of Lum Chang Securities, a member of the SES.
"Now that a local firm is involved and it is a member of the exchange, SES will have to investigate as Lum is also chairman of the company," said one source.
A SES spokesman declined comment when contacted by Reuters.
Lum, who is also chairman of the publicly listed Lum Chang Holdings Ltd, the holding company for Lum Chang Securities, was not immediately available for comment.
A Lum Chang official said the company would issue a statement later in the day.

Lum has been charged with insider trading by the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). The charges relate to the proposed takeover by Singapore-based Neptune Orient Lines (NOL) of U.S.-based APL Ltd.
Singapore newspaper reports said Lum sent a fax in his personal capacity over the weekend denying the SEC charges and saying he "will strenously resist the spurious allegations".
Lum is the third person, and the second Singaporean, charged by the SEC for insider trading of APL shares.
The SEC said Lum opened a trading account on February 25 and between then and March 18 bought 190,100 APL shares for $4.4 million.
The SEC alleged that Lum made an illegal profit after APL shares rose sharply on April 14, one day after the company announced that it would be acquired by NOL for $825 million.
The agency also noted that Lum bought the shares one day after the SES was informed of the planned takeover of APL.
An industry source, who declined to be identified, said SES members would not have been given information which was not meant for for public disclosure.

"If information is passed on to the SES for disclosure, the exchange will be obliged to disseminate the information. But if the information was not meant for public disclosure, member firms will not be informed," said the source.
